subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should Skill Workshop have a core-owned machine-readable lifecycle contract, and should that contract be OpenClaw-native, AISP/AISOP reference material, or kept outside core?
rationale: The request is technically plausible but sets product and security direction for a governance surface that controls generated skill writes, scanner gates, rollback, and target boundaries.

options.title: Adopt OpenClaw-native contract first
options.body: Document the lifecycle invariants as a core reference/test fixture, mirror them in focused tests, and keep AISP/AISOP illustrative with no runtime authority.

options.title: Route as ClawHub or bundle reference
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core on the existing service/docs/tests and let an optional external package describe the lifecycle without becoming a core contract.

options.title: Decline contract artifact for now
options.body: Treat current docs, schemas, service tests, and related runtime-validation issues as sufficient until a concrete validator or trace consumer exists.

recommendation.title: Adopt OpenClaw-native contract first
recommendation.body: Document the lifecycle invariants as a core reference/test fixture, mirror them in focused tests, and keep AISP/AISOP illustrative with no runtime authority.

likelyOwner.reason: The central Skill Workshop proposal store, CLI, and Gateway history traces to Shakker-authored commits, so this is the strongest code-history routing candidate.
